header.running_head: Hadhrat Zubayr bin Awwaam (RA) Distributes Wealth

blocks.text: 'A hundred thousand.' He then said, 'By Allaah! I do not think that you have enough money for that.' I said, 'What would you say if it was two million, two hundred thousand?' He replied, 'I do not think that you would ever be able to settle it. Nevertheless, if you need any assistance, do not hesitate to ask me.'" Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) had purchased the piece of land in Ghaabah for one hundred and seventy thousand. Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) evaluated its value to be one million, six hundred thousand (he then divided it into sixteen parts, each worth a hundred thousand). He then made the announcement, "Whoever has a debt due from Zubayr should meet us at Ghaabah." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) came up. He was owed a sum of a hundred thousand. He said to Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA), "If you please, I could write off the debt." "No," replied Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA). "Otherwise," said Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA), "if you so wish, you could include me amongst those who are the last to be paid." When Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) did not agree to this either, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) asked to be given a piece of the land in settlement. Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) then gave him a piece of the land saying, "You may have the land from this point to this point." Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) then sold the other pieces of land and settled all the debts in full. At the end, there were only four and a half properties left (from the sixteen). Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) then approached Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) who was then in the company of Hadhrat Amr bin Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Mundhir bin Zubayr (RA) and Hadhrat Ibn Zam'ah (RA). "How much did you evaluate the property at Ghaabah to be?" When Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) informed him that each portion was valued at a hundred thousand, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) asked how many portions were still available. "Four and a half," replied Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA). "I shall take one portion for a hundred thousand," said Hadhrat Mundhir bin Zubayr (RA). "And I shall take another for a hundred thousand," said Hadhrat Amr bin Uthmaan (RA). "I too shall take one for a hundred thousand," said Hadhrat Ibn Zam'ah (RA). Hadhrat Mu'aawiya then asked, "How many does that leave?" "One and a half portions," replied Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA). "I shall take them for a hundred and fifty thousand," said Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA). Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ja'far (RA) also sold his portion of the land to Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) for six hundred thousand. When Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) had settled all the debts, the children of Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) asked for their inheritance to be distributed. However, Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) refused and said, "By Allaah! I shall not distribute anything amongst you until I make an announcement during four Hajj seasons calling all people who were owed any money by (our father) Zubayr (RA)." He then made the announcement during four consecutive years during the Hajj season. It was only after the fourth year that he finally distributed the inheritance (amongst his brothers and sisters).
